question: Can two declared sound finite observations strictly reduce a fixed candidate set while retaining its stipulated true point, and what happens under repetition, conflict or incomplete coverage?
arithmetic: integer pairs (i,j), interpreted as rational coordinates (i/n,j/n)
candidate_family: i>=0, j>=0, i+j<=n; n=16 or 12 only
assumptions: Each interval is a sound observation of the same fixed object in the same coordinate frame. True points are stipulated synthetic oracles, not inferred from peer reports.
protected: retain true points when both observations are sound
no strict reduction from duplicate constraints
success: Compare full enumeration to independently parameterized sum/difference inverse; retain truth; pass controls and new-instance reuse; replay serialized evidence.
enforcement: Unix alarm, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_AS, explicit visit counter and serialized-output byte limit. No subprocesses, network or input code execution.
exit: Stop after the two fixed instances and controls; limits produce Unknown. This is one finite calibration, not a universal convergence or speedup claim.
